“The unexamined life is not worth living.” — Socrates

It is possible to spend years working, planning, meeting obligations and moving forward without asking one fundamental question: where is all of this actually taking me?

For Socrates, examining life did not mean endlessly doubting yourself. It meant being willing to question your decisions, beliefs and values. Why am I choosing this path? Is this genuinely what I want? What matters to me, and what am I doing simply because it has become familiar?

Sometimes one honest answer to yourself can change more than dozens of answers given by others.

“The unexamined life is not worth living.” — Socrates

We can spend years moving forward without ever seriously asking ourselves: Where am I going, and why?

Socrates reminds us that examining life means paying attention to our choices, beliefs, mistakes and what genuinely matters to us.

Sometimes the most important conversation is the honest one we have with ourselves.
